1976 Tehran UFO incident

#ufo #ufotwitter 

This is one of the most well-documented UFO cases involving military aircraft, radar, visual sightings, and electromagnetic interference effects.

Key Details of the Incident (September 19, 1976)

Location: Over Tehran, Iran (then under the Shah's regime).
Time: Early morning hours, starting around 12:30 AM local time.
Initial Reports: Multiple civilian calls to authorities about strange bright objects in the sky (some described as bird-like or helicopter-like with lights; no helicopters were airborne).
Response: Iranian Air Force scrambled F-4 Phantom II jets from Shahrokhi Air Force Base to intercept.

A first F-4 approached the primary object (visible from ~70 miles away as a brilliant light). At ~25 nautical miles, the pilot lost all instrumentation and communications (UHF and intercom). Systems returned when he broke off and turned away.

A second F-4 was launched. The backseater achieved radar lock at 27 NM (object at 12 o'clock high, closing slowly). The object was described as intensely bright with flashing strobe lights in a rectangular pattern (alternating blue, green, red, orange—so fast that all colors appeared visible simultaneously). Radar return size was comparable to a Boeing 707 tanker.

The object maintained distance (~25 NM). A smaller object (1/3 to 1/2 the apparent size of the moon) detached from the primary, headed rapidly toward the F-4. The pilot tried to launch an AIM-9 Sidewinder missile, but the weapons control panel failed, and he lost all communications. He evaded by turning and diving; the smaller object followed briefly before rejoining the primary.

Another object detached and descended rapidly to the ground, landing gently (no explosion) and illuminating an area 2–3 km in radius with bright light. The F-4 crew observed this while descending from 25,000 to 15,000 ft; they experienced UHF/instrument interference when passing certain magnetic bearings relative to Tehran.

On approach back to Mehrabad Airport, the crew sighted yet another cylinder-shaped object (about the size of a T-bird jet) at ~10,000 ft with bright steady lights on each end and a flasher in the middle. Tower confirmed no known traffic.

Daylight follow-up: A helicopter search of the supposed landing site (a dry lake bed) detected a beeper signal near a small house. Residents reported a loud noise and bright light "like lightning." Radiation checks were conducted on the area and aircraft (results not detailed in the initial report; more info promised but not followed up in this doc).

Notable Aspects

Electromagnetic effects: Repeated instrumentation/comms failures and weapons malfunctions when approaching or attempting to engage the object(s).

Credibility: Reported by trained military pilots and controllers; corroborated by radar locks and multiple witnesses. The U.S. Defense Intelligence Agency (DIA) forwarded the details widely, including to the White House, Secretary of State, CIA, NSA, Joint Chiefs of Staff, and various military commands—indicating significant interest (though U.S. officials later called the distribution routine for sensitive Middle East reports).

In my opinion, I'm quite sure it was either an American or a Russian electromagnetic vehicle.
